[id 0]: The passage explicitly states that on the accordion you do *not* need to hit the keys with a lot of force for extra volume (unlike piano), and instead you use the bellows. Therefore option A is the inaccurate tip.  
[id 1]: The passage says borders are cut “to ensure that the image covers the whole screen.” That matches option B.  
[id 2]: The colony begins a nomadic phase “when available food has decreased,” and during this phase they march at night and camp during the day, changing nests daily. So option B is true.  
[id 3]: The passage describes biological clocks as “self sustaining oscillators which will continue a period of free-running cycling even in the absence of external cues.” They are the entities that keep going independently, so option C is correct.  
[id 4]: Visiting a science museum is not an on-site natural-area activity; the passage lists outdoor/nature activities like fishing, photography, and visiting parks. Option C is the outlier.  
[id 5]: A five-bit binary number must have exactly five digits that are only 0 or 1. Option C (10010) fits.  
[id 6]: The passage says the audience’s presence motivates students to improve writing to *avoid* criticism; it does not claim that criticism actually decreases. Thus option B is not mentioned as a benefit.  
[id 7]: The passage mentions jousts, chivalry, and dungeon pits, but never explicitly mentions “knights.” Option D is correct.
